rubrics.justification: The response appropriately notes this is a static-image approximation and reasonably identifies a blastocyst with suboptimal ICM/TE, but the exact expansion stage and grading are somewhat uncertain from the image and may overstate visibility of a distinct ICM and full blastocoel.

It integrates maternal age, ovarian reserve, BMI, tubal factor, prior IVF outcome, sperm parameters, and endometrial thickness well, and explains how favorable patient factors may offset moderate embryo morphology.

The reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with morphology driving prognosis and patient factors modifying it; only minor uncertainty exists around the exact morphology-to-probability mapping.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice guidelines, including SET at age 33, attention to hydrosalpinx, uterine cavity review, and cautious use of PGT-A; minor limitation is the somewhat confident grading from a single image.

Provides clear practical next steps for current transfer and future planning, including SET, hydrosalpinx assessment, luteal support adherence, uterine cavity evaluation, lab review, and when to consider PGT-A.
